output.best_reason: Version A has the most distinct voice and the most controlled tension. The clock motif runs through the whole interview, so the alibi details feel like evidence rather than a list. Its refusal to name a time of death ("I will not give you a time I cannot prove") and the closing cigar-case beat, which quietly re-examines his own movements, keep the reader suspicious. Its period texture comes through diction and detail (the temple bell, piquet, the pastor's daughter) rather than costume, so it avoids pastiche. Version B is close behind: it is crisp, the Chopin and mantel-clock details are handled naturally, and its questions pace the facts well. Version D is witty and has a strong ending, but its jokes and Latin tags are a little too polished, and the mallet detail is a fact the other versions don't carry. Version C is the warmest, but it leans on sentiment ("God forgive me," "a foolish old man"), reads more like a eulogy than an interrogation, and generates the least tension.
